title: The Prompt is the Platform - Dominik Tornow, Resonate HQ
talk_summary: Dominik Tornow argues that as agents can generate implementations on demand, the reusable product becomes the specification, not the code. He describes a pipeline of abstract spec → deterministic simulation → concrete spec → concrete implementation, where a Python deterministic simulator with injected stale reads and 'forbidden fruit' trace events lets agents design correct distributed algorithms before writing production code.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic simulation environment for agent-designed algorithms
takeaways.what_they_do: They built a Python simulator of the target platform (NATS KV) that deterministically injects stale reads and enforces optimistic concurrency, so failures are repeatable and inspectable rather than flaky.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the simulation is deterministic, it's repeatable, and it's inspectable

takeaways.what_they_do: The simulator records facts the production code cannot see (e.g., that a read was stale and what the latest value was) and exposes them only in traces, so the agent learns why an invariant broke, not just that it broke.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the algorithm is not allowed to depend on this information, but the agent is allowed to use it to explain why the algorithm it designed was wrong

takeaways.technique: Insert a concrete specification artifact between abstract spec and implementation
takeaways.what_they_do: When direct abstract-spec-to-code failed (happy path only, broke on concurrency/failure), they inserted an interactively derived concrete spec (schema, indices, queries, transaction boundaries) before implementation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead of asking the agent to jump directly from abstract spec to concrete implementation, we inserted an intermediary artifact, the concrete specification.

takeaways.technique: Simulation-first design phase driven by the agent
takeaways.what_they_do: They task the agent to build a simulated implementation ('executable design') to discover the correct algorithm under partial failure, then derive the concrete spec, then the production implementation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Do not build the production system. Build a simulated implementation.

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat the specification/protocol as the product and derive multiple implementations from it, making the spec the thing to verify repeatedly rather than each implementation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The product is no longer the implementation. The product is the specification, the protocol.
